_what_this_is: A complete, verbatim export of the NeuBit dashboard builder's live store (the Postgres database `neubit_dashboards`) — every dashboard, every widget on it, and every saved version — taken immediately before the builder was deleted from this repository.
_why_it_exists: NeuBit retired its own dashboard builder in favour of DashForge, the sibling product that is now this platform's single dashboarding surface. Deleting the `dashboards` service also ends the life of its database, and the rows below are not test fixtures: a person sat down and built `Building Overview` on 2026-08-30 and kept editing it for four hours. Code deletion is recoverable from git; a dropped database is not. This file is what makes the removal a migration rather than a loss — it carries enough to rebuild these widgets in DashForge with the old service gone, which is why it also resolves the point UUIDs the specs reference into human-readable device/point tags (see `referenced_points`) and restates each spec in plain English (see `reconstruction_notes`). The raw rows are kept alongside, unmodified, because a summary somebody wrote is not evidence and the raw row is.
_taken_from: docker compose (deploy/) → postgres → database `neubit_dashboards`, schema at alembic revision 0003_dashboard_versions
_source_of_truth_for_the_schema: backend/dashboards/app/dashboards/models.py at commit 55c0792 — read it in git history if a column below needs interpreting. Geometry (x/y/w/h) is in GRID CELLS, not pixels: x/w are in units of `grid_cols` across the canvas width, y/h in units of `row_height` pixels.
_two_spec_grammars_live_here: Widget specs are versioned and BOTH versions are present in this export. spec_version 1 is the original IoT-shaped grammar (`query.scope` of points/device/category/all + a single `metric`). spec_version 2 is the domain-agnostic grammar (`query.dataset` + `select`/`group_by`/`having`/`order_by`) described in docs/dashboard-builder-contract.md. The builder upgraded a v1 spec on read and never rewrote the stored row, so a widget untouched since before the v2 migration is still stored as v1. Do not assume one grammar when rebuilding.
_completeness: These counts are the FULL contents of the three tables, not a filtered selection — no WHERE clause was used. Note for anyone comparing against the removal brief, which said 8 stored versions: the live table held 7 (`version` 1 through 7, no gaps). 7 is what was there and 7 is what is here.
